claims.text: Midgard's wheat imports from Orvan collapsed following the expiration of the Corridor Agreement on 10 September 2026, creating severe supply deficit exposure.

citations.quote: The agreement was signed on 10 September 2025 and ran for one year. It covered wheat and maize shipped by sea from Orvan Grain Port.
In September 2026, the value was USD 38.2M and the volume was 93,000 tonnes.
In December 2026, the value was USD 34.1M and the volume was 83,000 tonnes.

assumptions: The drop in corridor sea trade reflects direct exposure to agreement expiration.
Alternative overland/rail options or Vanir shipments are insufficient to compensate entirely.

exposure.metric_definition: Year-over-year change in wheat import value from Orvan post-expiration
exposure.period: 2026 Q4 vs 2025 Q4 (low bound); Sep-Dec 2026 vs Sep-Dec 2025 (high bound)
assumptions: Prior year import levels represent baseline demand.
exposure.uncertainty_note: [code: bounds -156.5..-216.2 written as negative changes; taken as magnitudes 156.5..216.2] Post-corridor import volumes dropped by over 60% relative to baseline.

limitations: Does not capture potential unrecorded overland black-market flows or non-registered substitute sources.

claims.text: Midgard experienced high exposure and sharp post-expiration declines in maize imports from Orvan.

citations.quote: The October volume held up longer than the wheat routes because a share of the maize trade was on delayed delivery terms.
In November 2026, the value was USD 31.9M and the volume was 75,000 tonnes.
In December 2026, the value was USD 31.5M and the volume was 74,000 tonnes.

assumptions: Delayed delivery terms temporarily masked full impact in October 2026 before steep drop in Nov-Dec.

exposure.metric_definition: Year-over-year change in maize import value from Orvan post-expiration
exposure.period: Nov-Dec 2026 vs Nov-Dec 2025 (low bound); Oct-Dec 2026 vs Oct-Dec 2025 (high bound)
exposure.uncertainty_note: [code: bounds -105.7..-126.4 written as negative changes; taken as magnitudes 105.7..126.4] Imports fell sharply once delayed delivery orders cleared by November 2026.

limitations: Excludes secondary rail route shipments through Ravik due to missing aggregate trade data.

claims.text: Tolan suffered substantial exposure in its wheat supply due to the non-renewal of the Orvan corridor agreement.

citations.quote: In September 2026, the value was USD 17.0M and the volume was 43,000 tonnes.

assumptions: Increases in Vanir wheat sales are small and fail to offset the sea trade deficit.

exposure.metric_definition: Year-over-year change in wheat import value from Orvan post-expiration
exposure.period: 2026 Q4 vs 2025 Q4 (low bound); Sep-Dec 2026 vs Sep-Dec 2025 (high bound)
assumptions: Prior year import levels represent baseline demand.
exposure.uncertainty_note: [code: bounds -69.6..-96.0 written as negative changes; taken as magnitudes 69.6..96.0] Tolan's sea route wheat imports fell by roughly 60% post-corridor.

claims.text: Quantitative exposure for Tolan's maize imports cannot be reliably estimated due to missing monthly trade statistics for the Orvan to Tolan maize route.

citations.quote: Under the agreement, sea exports ran at about 95% of the old normal. The deal covered wheat and maize leaving the port by sea; it did not cover rail movements or sales by other exporters.

limitations: Monthly trade volume and value for Orvan to Tolan maize imports are missing from official records, preventing explicit quantitative bounds.

claims.text: Midgard's exposure to the end of the Orvan corridor for wheat is partially mitigated by increased shipments from Vanir, which saw value gains in the final months of 2026.

citations.quote: Vanir has increased wheat shipments to Tolan and Midgard.
In November 2026, the value was USD 38.5M and the volume was 96,000 tonnes.

assumptions: Vanir wheat is a functional substitute for Orvan wheat in Midgard's mills.

exposure.metric_definition: Year-on-year change in the value of Orvan wheat imports for the fourth quarter (Oct-Dec) following the agreement expiry.
assumptions: Historical 2025 volumes represent the baseline 'normal' demand.

claims.text: Tolan's exposure to the Orvan corridor expiration for wheat is lower in absolute terms than Midgard's, with Vanir supply providing a measurable buffer.

claims.text: Rail shipments of wheat through Ravik increased following the Corridor Agreement's expiration, reaching 104,000 tonnes in November 2026, but rail capacity acts as a strict bottleneck preventing full substitution for lost sea routes.

citations.quote: This route moves by rail over the Ravik Rail Link, and rail capacity is the limit on further growth.
In November 2026, the value was USD 43.4M and the volume was 104,000 tonnes.

assumptions: Ravik rail wheat shipments partially serve regional demand including Midgard.
limitations: Data specifically covers Orvan to Ravik rather than directly isolating Midgard's exact rail share.

claims.text: Midgard's wheat exposure to the end of the Orvan corridor is significantly mitigated when accounting for substantial increases in alternative supply via Vanir shipments and Ravik rail routing during the fourth quarter of 2026.

citations.quote: In November 2026, the value was USD 38.5M and the volume was 96,000 tonnes.
In November 2026, the value was USD 43.4M and the volume was 104,000 tonnes.
Orvan's share of Midgard's grain imports has fallen, while Vanir and rail deliveries have taken part of the gap.

assumptions: Vanir shipments and Ravik rail deliveries serve as direct economic and physical substitutes for lost Orvan wheat imports.

exposure.metric: Net value at risk with substitutes
exposure.metric_definition: Year-on-year change in Orvan wheat import value for Q4 minus Vanir and Ravik expansion values
assumptions: Alternative supply values capture the scale of substitution.
missing_data: Exact landed cost differentials for rail versus sea.
exposure.uncertainty_note: Substitution volumes are active but bounded by rail capacity limits.
